note: Nevada has no single child abuse hotline. Clark County and Washoe County each run their own, and the Division of Child and Family Services covers everywhere else - and in those rural counties, out of hours, the Division tells you to call local law enforcement instead. Nevada's board websites were also mid-reorganisation when this was checked, and several published complaint forms had gone; where that is the case the phone number and address below came from the board's own live page, and it is worth asking them to send you the current form.

civil_injury.summary: Two years. The same two-year limit covers assault, battery and false imprisonment, and personal injury caused by negligence.
civil_injury.quote: 4. Within 2 years: ... (c) An action for libel, slander, assault, battery, false imprisonment or seduction. ... (e) Except as otherwise provided in NRS 11.215 or 11.217, an action to recover damages for injuries to a person ... caused by the wrongful act or neglect of another.
civil_injury.note: 11.215 and 11.217 are the sexual abuse/assault rules, not covered here. 11.190 was last amended in 2025 (history line ends '2025, 2317'); the 2-year periods are unchanged.

civil_minor_tolling.summary: Yes. Time while you are under 18 does not count, so the two years usually run to your 20th birthday. Time spent in the State's custodial care (for example foster care or a state placement begun before 18) also does not count, unless the person is imprisoned, paroled or on probation. No general extended period for physical (non-sexual) child abuse.
civil_minor_tolling.quote: at the time the cause of action accrued, either: 1. Within the age of 18 years; or 2. Insane; or 3. In the custodial care of the State, if placed in such care while less than 18 years of age ... the time of such disability shall not be a part of the time limited
civil_minor_tolling.note: The custodial-care toll is directly relevant to state-placed youth: the clock may not start until they leave state care. Whether that includes youth placed by a county juvenile court or by another state was not researched.

civil_government_claims.summary: A tort claim against the State of Nevada is filed with the Attorney General, and against a county, city or other political subdivision with its governing body, within two years; filing that administrative claim is not a precondition to suing, and the lawsuit itself follows the normal two-year limit.
civil_government_claims.quote: 1. Each person who has a claim against the State or any of its agencies arising out of a tort must file the claim within 2 years after the time the cause of action accrues with the Attorney General. ... 3. The filing of a claim ... is not a condition precedent to bringing an action
civil_government_claims.note: Damages against the state and political subdivisions are capped by NRS 41.035 (not researched here). Suits against the government proceed under NRS 41.031.

criminal_child_abuse.summary: Three years from the offense for felony child abuse or neglect. For physical abuse there is no pause until the child turns 18; the longer child-victim deadlines (age 36 or 43) apply only to sexual abuse and sex trafficking. If the abuse was committed in a secret manner, the three years start when it is discovered.
criminal_child_abuse.quote: 4. Any felony other than the felonies listed in subsections 1, 2 and 3 must be found, or an information or complaint filed, within 3 years after the commission of the offense.
criminal_child_abuse.note: NRS 200.508 (https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NRS/NRS-200.html): willfully causing a child under 18 'unjustifiable physical pain or mental suffering as a result of abuse or neglect' is a category B felony whether or not substantial harm results. 171.095(1)(a): 'If a felony ... is committed in a secret manner', the period runs 'after the discovery of the offense'.

criminal_felony_assault.summary: Three years from the offense for felony battery or assault. Gross misdemeanors: two years. Misdemeanor battery or assault: one year.
criminal_felony_assault.quote: 1. A gross misdemeanor must be found, or an information or complaint filed, within 2 years after the commission of the offense. 2. Any other misdemeanor must be found, or an information or complaint filed, within 1 year after the commission of the offense.
criminal_felony_assault.note: The felony period (3 years) is quoted under criminal_child_abuse from the same section, 171.085(4). The secret-manner discovery rule in 171.095(1)(a) also applies to assault.

channels.name: Nevada Board of Examiners for Marriage and Family Therapists and Clinical Professional Counselors
channels.what_it_can_do: Takes complaints against Nevada marriage and family therapists, clinical professional counselors, their interns, and anyone else under its jurisdiction including allegations of unlicensed practice, and disciplines licences.
channels.who_to_report: An LMFT or CPC in Nevada, an intern working under one, or somebody practising without the licence.
channels.how: The complaint must be in writing and signed by you, and posted with your supporting documents. Ask the Board for its current complaint form.
channels.phone_note: Walk-in, phone and email hours are Tuesday to Thursday, 9am to 4pm only.
channels.mail: Board of Examiners for Marriage and Family Therapists and Clinical Professional Counselors, 500 N. Rainbow Boulevard, Suite 201, Las Vegas, NV 89107

channels.name: Nevada Board of Psychological Examiners
channels.what_it_can_do: Reviews and disciplines complaints against licensed psychologists in Nevada.
channels.how: Complete the Board's complaint form, and the Release of Psychological Records form where it applies, with as much detail and supporting documentation as you can. Complaints cannot be taken by phone - they must be in writing.
channels.mail: Nevada Board of Psychological Examiners, 3080 South Durango Drive, Suite 102, Las Vegas, NV 89117

channels.name: Nevada Board of Examiners for Social Workers
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines social workers in Nevada, including licensed clinical social workers. It calls the process filing an accusation of wrongdoing.
channels.who_to_report: An LCSW or other licensed social worker.
channels.how: File an accusation of wrongdoing through the Board's consumer page, which also sets out the disciplinary laws and regulations it works to.

channels.name: Nevada Bureau of Health Care Quality and Compliance (HCQC)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses, certifies and investigates health care facilities in Nevada, including facilities for the treatment of alcohol and drug abuse and residential psychiatric facilities. Investigators use interviews, records reviews and in-person observation.
channels.who_to_report: An HCQC-licensed facility - complaints about patient care or about how the facility is run.
channels.how: Call the complaint intake line; a message can be left at any hour and calls are returned within 48 to 72 hours. A complaint form can also be faxed to 702-486-6520.
channels.phone_note: Complaint intake. Messages can be left 24/7; calls returned in 48 to 72 hours.
channels.note: You may give your name or stay anonymous, and if you give it you can ask that it be kept confidential during the investigation. Every complaint is triaged by how much harm it suggests: a serious one can start an investigation within 48 hours, a lesser one waits for staff to be free.

channels.name: Nevada child abuse and neglect reporting
channels.what_it_can_do: Starts a child protective services investigation. Which agency takes the report depends on the county.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Nevada program. Report to the county the program is in: Clark County (Las Vegas and Henderson) on 702-399-0081, Washoe County (Reno and Sparks) on 833-900-7233, and the Division of Child and Family Services for every other county on 833-571-1041.
channels.how: Call the number for that county. In the rural counties, out of hours and at weekends, the Division tells you to call local law enforcement to make the report instead. In an emergency, 911.
channels.phone_note: Division of Child and Family Services, for counties other than Clark and Washoe.

channels.name: Nevada Disability Advocacy and Law Center
channels.what_it_can_do: Nevada's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Nevada program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
